about: Scrim SVG allow-list cases (docs/transfer/specs/svg-allowlist.md). Every expectation was produced by running Scrim's own code, not written by hand.

sources.inline: packages/core/src/svg.ts svgContentIssues via applyPatch(addNode(box "Icon" id "v" with svg)) (core patch.ts checkSvg); markup = svgMarkup(svgTree(svg, "svg-v"))
sources.file: packages/mcp/src/assets/sniff.ts sniffImage(bytes) (the import gate for .svg files); svgRefusal(text) shown separately
sources.pathEdit: packages/core/src/vector/path.ts parsePath(d) then serializePath(segs); writeIssues = svgContentIssues of a one-path svg with that d

conventions.layer: "inline": structured vector data on a node (JSON; the svg field). "file": the text (or bytes) of an imported .svg file. "pathEdit": path data parsed for path edit mode. "editRefusal": whether path edit mode can open the vector.
conventions.expect: "accept" | { refuse: "<verbatim message>" } | { normalised: "<verbatim output>" }. inline refuse = the PatchError message (node name "Icon" prefixed, at most 5 issues joined by "; ", then " (and N more)"); file refuse = the AssetError message; pathEdit refuse is the literal "parsePath: null" (the parser returns null and shows no message); pathEdit normalised = serializePath output; inline normalised = the generated markup.
conventions.issues: inline only: every issue svgContentIssues returns, unprefixed (the first 20 when there are more).
conventions.nodeType: inline only: the node type the svg is written on (default "box").
conventions.markup: inline accept only (small cases): the markup Scrim generates for that svg on node id "v".
conventions.code: file refuse only: the AssetError code.
conventions.bytes: file only: the byte length of the materialised input.
conventions.sniffed: file accept only: { ext, width, height, orientation } as sniffImage reports.
conventions.svgRefusal: file only: svgRefusal(text) — the bare reason before ": Scrim imports only self-contained SVGs" is appended (null: nothing found).
conventions.writeIssues: pathEdit only: what the write-time check says about a one-path svg with this d (empty: accepted on write).

generate.what: Large inputs are stored as a generator; materialise them before running. target is a dot path into svg ("" = svg itself; "children.0.d" = svg.children[0].d).
generate.repeat-string: set target to prefix + unit repeated count times + suffix
generate.repeat-element: set target to an array of count deep copies of element; with elementString, each copy's elementString.target is first set to its prefix + unit×count + suffix
generate.nest: set target to prefix + open×count + inner + close×count + suffix
generate.nest-g: set target to [ g ] nested depth times around [ leaf ]: depth 1 = [{ tag: "g", children: [leaf] }]

conventions.file svg as bytes: a file case whose svg is { bytes: [...] } is raw bytes (not valid UTF-8).
